cues.zh: 那么，我们先从 GIL 的历史讲起。

cues.en: The GIL was added in 1992.
cues.zh: GIL 是在 1992 年引入的。

cues.en: Guido wanted to add support for this new thing that operating systems are starting to do called threading,
cues.zh: 当时 Guido 想支持操作系统刚兴起的一个新概念——线程，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 并且，

cues.en: he needed a way of protecting the global and static variables inside of CPython so that you couldn't have races between multiple threads, and so he added this thing called the GILT
cues.zh: 他需要一种方法来保护 CPython 内部的全局和静态变量，避免多线程之间的竞争，于是他加入了这个叫 GIL 的东西——

cues.en: twenty four years ago. And
cues.zh: 那是 24 年前的事了。而且，

cues.en: let's make no mistake,
cues.zh: 不可否认的是，

cues.en: this was a lovely design and it has served us very well, that has a lot of wonderful positive attributes.
cues.zh: 这在当时是非常精妙的设计，它多年来一直很好地服务着我们，并且具备很多出色的优点。

cues.en: I'm not in the camp of gil haters. I think that that's...
cues.zh: 我不是反对 GIL 的阵营。我觉得……

cues.en: I think people who are gil haters are kind of misinformed.
cues.zh: 我觉得那些反感 GIL 的人其实有点误解了。

cues.en: So let's talk about the ramifications of this design.
cues.zh: 所以我们来聊聊这个设计的影响。

cues.en: First of all, the GIL was incredibly simple, which meant it was easy to get right, both for us and it was easy for C Python...
cues.zh: 首先，GIL 极其简单，这意味着它很容易实现正确，无论是对我们还是对 CPython 来说……

cues.en: C extension authors to get right.
cues.zh: 对 C 扩展的作者来说也很容易搞定。

cues.en: It had no deadlocks because there's only one lock, so you can't have deadlocks between two locks because there aren't two locks.
cues.zh: 它不会产生死锁，因为只有一个锁，所以你不会在两个锁之间死锁，因为根本没有第二个锁。

cues.en: It had very
cues.zh: 它几乎

cues.en: little overhead. You touch the GIL infrequently.
cues.zh: 没有什么开销。你很少需要去操作 GIL。

cues.en: And if you had
cues.zh: 而且如果你运行的是

cues.en: single threaded code,
cues.zh: 单线程代码，

cues.en: it ran incredibly fast because, again, we didn't have any synchronization overhead, we didn't have any locking and unlocking.
cues.zh: 它的运行速度会快得惊人，因为同样地，我们没有任何同步开销，也没有任何加锁和解锁的操作。

cues.en: Your code just ran.
cues.zh: 你的代码直接就能跑。

cues.en: Almost no overhead. And it ensured that it sort of paved the way for your code to run very, very quickly.
cues.zh: 几乎零开销。而且它确保了为你的代码实现极速运行铺平了道路。

cues.en: If
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: your program is IO bound and you use multiple threads, then everything worked great, and this is actually the original use case of threading because computers didn't develop multiple cores until very recently, or at least, you know, consumer
cues.zh: 你的程序是 I/O 密集型并且使用了多线程，那么一切都运行良好，这其实也是线程最初的使用场景，因为直到最近计算机才发展出多核，或者至少，你知道的，消费级

cues.en: level hardware.
cues.zh: 硬件。

cues.en: The problem is, of course, if you run multiple threads and your program is CPU bound, you're kind of out of luck. The GIL ensures that your code is only going to run on a single core at a time,
cues.zh: 当然，问题在于，如果你运行多线程并且你的程序是 CPU 密集型，那你可就有点走运不佳了。GIL 确保了你的代码在同一时间只能在一个核心上运行，

cues.en: which was fine in 1992. It was rare that you would see a multicore computer back then, but the world has changed around us over the subsequent
cues.zh: 这在 1992 年完全没问题。那时候多核电脑很少见，但在此后的

cues.en: twenty four years. So these days, wonderfully thin and light laptops
cues.zh: 二十四年里，我们周围的世界已经变了。所以如今，轻薄得惊人的笔记本电脑、

cues.en: and our phones
cues.zh: 我们的手机、

cues.en: and our watches and our eyeglasses have all gone multicore.
cues.zh: 我们的手表和眼镜，全都已经走向了多核。

cues.en: We live in a deeply multicore world, and Python
cues.zh: 我们生活在一个深度多核的世界里，而 Python

cues.en: is is still doing single core.
cues.zh: 依然在使用单核。

cues.en: I have a workstation at home that has 28 cores in it. Like, I I want multicore stuff, but Python just isn't ready for it. This is a comment actually sitting in the Python source code right now.
cues.zh: 我家里有一台工作站有 28 个核。你看，我 我想要多核的东西，但 Python 还没准备好。这其实是目前 Python 源代码里的一条注释。

cues.en: My suggestion is that it's it's time to consider moving beyond rudimentary thread support. After all,
cues.zh: 我的建议是，是时候考虑超越最基本的线程支持了。毕竟，

cues.en: your computer has all these wonderful resources, and Python is able to take advantage of all of them,
cues.zh: 你的电脑拥有所有这些美妙的资源，Python 也能利用其中所有的资源，

cues.en: except for the multiple cores.
cues.zh: 除了多核。

cues.en: And this is kind of a sore point. A lot of people, yeah, if you have a problem, you can go multiprocess, then of course, yes, can take care of take advantage of the multiple cores, but there are definitely problem domains where that's not true, and those people would maybe love to use Python and they just kind of can't.
cues.zh: 这有点让人头疼。很多人会说，对吧，如果你遇到问题，你可以用多进程，那当然可以，能够利用多核，但确实存在一些问题领域并非如此，那些人可能很想用 Python，却只是用不了。

cues.en: Now there was an attempt to remove the GIL before, and when I say attempt, what I mean is they successfully removed the GIL.
cues.zh: 过去曾有过一次移除 GIL 的尝试，当我说尝试时，我的意思是他们成功地移除了 GIL。

cues.en: This was back in Python one point four days in 1999. It was literally like December 1999 the patch was posted, so right before the Y2K bug and everyone was nervous.
cues.zh: 那是 1999 年 Python 1.4 的时代。补丁发布时 literalmente（字面意思）是 1999 年 12 月，就在千年虫问题爆发前夕，所有人都很紧张。

cues.en: This change did not require changing the CAPI, so your code
cues.zh: 这个改动不需要修改 CAPI，所以你的代码

cues.en: usually
cues.zh: 通常

cues.en: would still just run.
cues.zh: 依然可以正常运行。

cues.en: It took all of those global variables that were in the Python core
cues.zh: 它把 Python 核心中所有那些

cues.en: that Guido was protecting with the GIL and moved them into a single struct called pythreadstate,
cues.zh: Guido 曾用 GIL 保护的全局变量移到了一个名为 pythreadstate 的结构体中，

cues.en: which we actually... That got merged. We have that today.
cues.zh: 实际上我们……那个被合并了。我们今天还在用它。

cues.en: It added a single mutex lock about... Around anchor and decker. On Windows, it used something smarter called interlocked increment.
cues.zh: 它在 Anchor 和 Decker 周围加了一把互斥锁……在 Windows 上，它用了更聪明的办法，叫作互锁递增。

cues.en: And it made your code between four and seven times slower. So again, I want to just make this point. The GIL makes your code run fast, and removing the GIL makes your code run more slowly, and that's the challenge of removing the GIL.
cues.zh: 这让你的代码慢了四到七倍。所以我再强调一下：GIL 能让代码运行得很快，移除 GIL 会让代码运行得更慢，而这正是移除 GIL 的难点。

cues.en: So if you want to know more about this free threading patch, David Beasley wrote a wonderful blog post called An Inside Look at the GIL Removal Patch of Lore. Very easy to find on the Internet.
cues.zh: 如果你想进一步了解这个自由线程补丁，David Beasley 写过一篇很棒的博客文章，叫《深入了解传说中的 GIL 移除补丁》。在网上很容易找到。

cues.en: I've referred to it a lot. But even that is 15 ago. I feel like it's time to try again, so I have this project I'm calling the galactomy.
cues.zh: 我经常提到它。但那也已经是 15 年前的事了。我觉得是时候再试一次了，所以我有个项目，叫作 Gilectomy。

cues.en: That's the surgical removal of the gill.
cues.zh: 这就是对 GIL 的外科式移除。

cues.en: And I've thought about the problem a lot. So I would say that there are four technical considerations you must take into account when you try to remove the gill. Those are reference counting, of course. Python objects are reference counts in order to keep track with their lifetimes. Very quickly,
cues.zh: 我花了很多时间思考这个问题。所以我认为，尝试移除 GIL 时，必须考虑四个技术因素。首先当然是引用计数。Python 对象通过引用计数来跟踪自己的生命周期。简单来说，

cues.en: if every Python object has a number associated with it called the reference count, if
cues.zh: 如果每个 Python 对象都有一个与之关联的数字，叫作引用计数，那么

cues.en: that object is stored in three places, like there's it's a member of a module
cues.zh: 如果这个对象被存放在三个地方，比如它是某个模块的成员，

cues.en: and it's stored in a list and something else, it'll have a reference count of three.
cues.zh: 又被存放在一个列表里，还存放在别的地方，那么它的引用计数就是三。

cues.en: Every time you drop your reference, like if you say, if you remove it from the list, then you decrement the reference count, and so it'd have a reference count of two. When the reference count reaches zero, you free the object because no one's interested anymore. So that's when you dell and that's when you reclaim the memory.
cues.zh: 每次你移除一个引用，比如把它从列表中移除，就会将引用计数减一，这样它的引用计数就变成二。当引用计数归零时，就会释放这个对象，因为已经没人再需要它了。这时你就会执行 del，也会回收这部分内存。

cues.en: Python objects use this and if you have multiple threads that are both trying to access the object at the same time, you could have a race between them trying to update the reference count. You could result in an incorrect reference count and then you're freeing memory too early or freeing it too late and it's a memory leak.
cues.zh: Python 对象会用到这个，如果多个线程同时尝试访问该对象，它们之间就可能产生竞争，试图更新引用计数。这可能导致引用计数出错，然后你就会过早释放内存，或者过晚释放导致内存泄漏。

cues.en: We need to address reference counting in order to run Python on multiple cores simultaneously.
cues.zh: 我们需要解决引用计数问题，才能让 Python 同时跑在多个核心上。

cues.en: Globals and static variables, there are a fair number of them, like specifically there's a bunch of per thread information that we would need to ensure
cues.zh: 全局变量和静态变量有不少，比如具体来说有一堆每个线程的信息，我们需要确保

cues.en: was kept separate, the different threads are kept separate from each other, and there are a bunch of shared singleton objects like a string or a module or the small integers. Python pre creates all the small integers and shares those. And those would, of course, need to work across multiple threads.
cues.zh: 它们保持分离，不同线程彼此隔离，还有一堆共享的单例对象，比如字符串、模块或小整数。Python 会预先创建所有小整数并共享它们。当然，这些都需要跨多线程正常工作。

cues.en: C extensions
cues.zh: C 扩展

cues.en: run-in a world right now, the GIL guarantees that a C extension will only ever run one thread at a time unless they explicitly say, You know what? Threads are okay right now.
cues.zh: 目前运行的世界里，GIL 保证 C 扩展一次只会运行一个线程，除非它们明确表示，你懂的？现在多线程是没问题的。

cues.en: A C extension has never lived in a world where more than one thread can be running inside of it at a time, and they make assumptions about this all the time, and allowing multiple threads to run inside of a C extension is going to break it, so we need to address that. And finally, the atomicity of operations.
cues.zh: C 扩展从未生活在多线程同时在其内部运行的世界里，它们一直对此做出假设，而允许多个线程在 C 扩展内运行会破坏它，所以我们需要解决这个问题。最后，操作的原子性。

cues.en: If you have a Python dict and you add to it or if you have a Python list and you append to it,
cues.zh: 如果你有一个Python字典并向其中添加内容，或者你有一个Python列表并向其追加元素，

cues.en: there are a bunch of steps that have to happen in order for that to occur.
cues.zh: 要完成这些操作，必须按顺序执行一系列步骤。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: in Python right now, we just guarantee that no other thread can interrupt you while you're doing those operations. But if we have multiple threads and a second thread tried to examine that object when you were in one of these incomplete states where you hadn't finished the append to the list, say,
cues.zh: 目前在Python中，我们只是保证在你执行这些操作时，没有其他线程能打断你。但如果我们有多个线程，而第二个线程试图在你处于这些未完成状态（比如你还没完成对列表的追加）时检查那个对象，

cues.en: it could see the object in an incomplete state. So we need to guarantee that objects don't examine...
cues.zh: 它可能会看到处于未完成状态的对象。所以我们需要保证对象不被检查……

cues.en: Other threads don't examine objects while they're in these incomplete states. We need to guarantee that those operations are atomic from the perspective of a Python program.
cues.zh: 其他线程不会在对象处于这些未完成状态时检查它们。我们需要保证，从Python程序的角度来看，这些操作是原子的。

cues.en: But in addition to these four technical considerations,
cues.zh: 但除了这四个技术方面的考虑，

cues.en: I say that there are three political considerations. Political,
cues.zh: 我认为还有三个政治方面的考虑。政治，

cues.en: kind of a bad word, but those are the best I could come up with. These are
cues.zh: 这个词不太好，但这是我所能想到的最好的说法。这些是

cues.en: not technical
cues.zh: 非技术

cues.en: considerations,
cues.zh: 方面的考虑，

cues.en: but these are considerations that are imposed on us by the community
cues.zh: 但这些是社区强加给我们的考虑，

cues.en: or by things that aren't necessarily a technical thing. So the first one, Guido has said... He wrote a blog post in 2007, I'll talk about later, where he said, I would welcome
cues.zh: 或者是由不一定是技术性的事情带来的。所以第一个，Guido说过……他在2007年写了一篇博客文章，我稍后会谈到，他说，我会欢迎

cues.en: a patch that removed the GIL only if it did not hurt single threaded code
cues.zh: 一个移除GIL的补丁，前提是它不损害单线程代码

cues.en: or it did not hurt multi threaded code that was IO bound.
cues.zh: 或者不损害IO密集型的多线程代码。

cues.en: That's a very high bar to reach.
cues.zh: 要达到这个标准可真不容易。

cues.en: I say that we also shouldn't break C extensions. We broke every C extension out there with the introduction of Python 3.0,
cues.zh: 我是说，我们也不该破坏 C 扩展。Python 3.0 的推出把我们现有的每一个 C 扩展都破坏了，

cues.en: and it's taken us a long time for the C extensions to get ported up to it. If we release a new version of Python, we say, we removed the GIL. You're welcome. Oh, all of your C extensions broke. You're welcome. People are going to get annoyed with us, so let's not do that. Let's not break the C extensions
cues.zh: C 扩展花了很长时间才移植过来。如果我们发布 Python 新版本，说我们移除了 GIL，不用谢。结果你所有的 C 扩展都坏了，不用谢。大家肯定会烦我们，所以别这么干，别弄坏 C 扩展。

cues.en: to the degree that we can preserve them.
cues.zh: 在能够保留它们的程度上。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: don't make it too complicated, and of course this is pretty fuzzy, but the idea here is that CPython is very easy to work on. The code is very clear, it's very straightforward, it's very easy to modify,
cues.zh: 别搞得太复杂，当然这很模糊，但这里的核心思想是 CPython 非常容易上手。代码非常清晰、直接，修改起来也很容易，

cues.en: it's very easy to read and understand and reason about. And if we complicate it by adding multi core support, then that's going to hurt our ability to
cues.zh: 它非常易读、易懂，也容易推导。如果我们因为加入多核支持把它搞复杂，那就会削弱我们去……的能力

cues.en: keep evolving in the future to modify it, fix bugs, maintain it, all those things. So let's try to minimize
cues.zh: 未来还要持续演进，去修改它、修 bug、维护它，诸如此类。所以我们要尽量减少

cues.en: the complexity that we introduce by getting rid of the GIL.
cues.zh: 我们通过摆脱GIL所引入的复杂性。

cues.en: So a quick detour. I want to talk about a couple of approaches I don't think will work. People have said for years, If only we could get rid of reference counting and go to
cues.zh: 那么简单绕个路。我想聊聊几种我认为行不通的方法。多年来人们一直说，要是我们能摆脱引用计数，转向

cues.en: the correct term is tracing garbage collection. This is what everybody else does. Java,
cues.zh: 正确的术语是追踪式垃圾回收。其他所有人都这么做。Java，

cues.en: C in the CLR,
cues.zh: CLR 中的 C，

cues.en: I think Rust, Go, D,
cues.zh: 我觉得 Rust、Go、D，

cues.en: all the modern languages use garbage collection to reclaim objects, to manage object lifetime. It's Python and just a couple others that use reference counting.
cues.zh: 所有现代语言都使用垃圾回收来回收对象、管理对象的生命周期。只有 Python 和另外寥寥几种语言使用引用计数。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: conventional wisdom is that garbage collection, tracing garbage collection, is about as fast as reference counting, so that's not going to hurt us. Where it hurts us is it's going to break all the C extensions. This is a major change to the API. All the C extensions work. It's also a more complicated API than reference counting. Reference counting is actually a very simple API, very easy to get right. And even there, we still have C extensions that are getting it wrong. It happens all the time. If we introduce an even more complicated API that C extension authors have to use, we're we're going to make it harder to write C extensions, we're going to make it harder for them to get it correct, which is really going to add bugs essentially.
cues.zh: 传统观点认为，垃圾回收，即追踪式垃圾回收，速度其实和引用计数差不多，所以这倒不会对我们造成影响。它真正伤害我们的地方在于，它会破坏所有的C扩展。这对API来说是一个重大的改变。所有的C扩展都得能运行。而且它比引用计数要复杂得多。引用计数其实是一个非常简单的API，非常容易正确实现。即便如此，我们依然有很多C extensions搞砸了。这种事经常发生。如果我们引入一个更复杂的API让C extension的作者们去使用，那么编写C扩展就会变得更难，他们要想正确实现也会更难，这实际上基本上就会引入各种Bug。

cues.en: So I would say I don't think we can consider this for now. Maybe it's something we could talk about in the future, but not now.
cues.zh: 所以我想说，目前我们还不能考虑这个。也许以后我们可以讨论，但现在不行。

cues.en: Software transactional memory, this is way cooler. This is the coolest thing. Software transactional memory is amazing,
cues.zh: 软件事务内存，这个酷多了。这才是最酷的东西。软件事务内存太棒了，

cues.en: but it's also very early. So if you followed the work at all of Armen Rigaud, he's been working on a branch of PyPI for a number of years to add software transactional memory. He's... When he walks in the room, he's the smartest person in the room. He's brilliant,
cues.zh: 但它也还处于非常早期的阶段。如果你关注过Armen Rigaud的工作，就会知道他一直在PyPI的一个分支上工作了好几年，试图加入软件事务内存。他是……当他走进房间时，他就是房间里最聪明的人。他才华横溢，

cues.en: and he's having trouble with it. I think us mortals don't have a chance. So
cues.zh: 然而他在处理这个时也遇到了麻烦。我觉得我们这些凡人就更没戏了。所以

cues.en: while performance would be amazing
cues.zh: 尽管性能会非常惊人，

cues.en: in software transactional memory and would fix all sorts of problems,
cues.zh: 而且软件事务内存能解决各种各样的问题，

cues.en: it would obviously break every C extension out there to a crazy degree because it has an incredibly complicated and hard to get right API.
cues.zh: 但它显然会极其严重地破坏现有的每一个C extension，因为它有一个极其复杂且很难正确实现的API。

cues.en: I asked Armin, was like, Could we put CPython on STM? And he was like, You don't want to do it. It's so hard to get right.
cues.zh: 我问 Armin，我说，我们能把 CPython 跑在 STM 上吗？他说，你绝对不想这么做，要把这搞定太难了。

cues.en: So I don't think that's approachable. So instead, let's talk about what I proposed with the Gillectomy.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得这行不通，那我们换个话题，聊聊我提出的“无 GIL 改造”（Gillectomy）。

cues.en: And I want to make it clear, by the way, so people say, Oh, you're removing the Gill. I'm like, no, I removed the GIL in April. Now I'm working on making it faster. So all of these things have happened, and I have a Python interpreter that doesn't have a GIL that can run some Python programs.
cues.zh: 顺便我想澄清一下，大家总说，“哦，你要移除 GIL 了。” 我会说，不，我在 4 月份就把 GIL 移除了，现在我正致力于让它变得更快。所以这些进展都已经实现了，我现在的 Python 解释器没有 GIL，并且能运行一些 Python 程序。

cues.en: Very few.
cues.zh: 虽然非常少。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: reference counting, we keep reference counting.
cues.zh: 引用计数，我们保留了引用计数。

cues.en: Reference counting, that's the API everybody expects, so it's not going to break any code,
cues.zh: 引用计数，这是每个人都期望的 API，所以它不会破坏任何代码，

cues.en: and it's going to... It is going to slow down. That's really the problem. I'm using something called Atomic Inger and Decker. This is functionality you get free with every Intel processor.
cues.zh: 而且它会……它确实会导致变慢。这才是真正的问题所在。我使用了一种叫原子增减（Atomic Inger and Decker）的技术。这是你买每个 Intel 处理器都免费附带的功能。

cues.en: This is the ability to add or subtract a number from any
cues.zh: 这就是能够对计算机内存中存储的任何

cues.en: integer stored in your computer's RAM in such a way that no other thread can fight you and have a race condition at the same time. It guarantees that this increment or decrement will be atomic,
cues.zh: 整数进行加减运算的能力，同时能确保没有其他线程会跟你冲突并产生竞态条件。它能保证这种增加或减少是原子的，

cues.en: but it costs us a lot. It's 30% slower off the top.
cues.zh: 但代价非常高。一上来性能就慢了 30%。

cues.en: I'm going to explore alternate approaches because this is hurting us a great deal with the golectomy.
cues.zh: 我打算探索其他替代方案，因为这严重拖慢了我们的无 GIL 改造。

cues.en: Globals and static variables, it turns out this wasn't really a big deal. First of all, the per thread stuff had already, years ago, been moved into this pythread state variable. I looked and I was like, oh, the work is done. I don't have to do anything here. These shared singletons, that's kind of the whole point of the golectomy. Python, everything is public all the time. In order for Python to work, you have to be able to share stuff between threads. So, yes, that's
cues.zh: 全局变量和静态变量，事实证明这其实不是什么大问题。首先，每个线程相关的东西在多年前就已经移到了这个 pythread state 变量中。我一看心想，哦，活儿已经干完了，我这里什么都不用做。至于这些共享的单例，这正是无 GIL 改造的核心意义所在。在 Python 中，所有东西随时都是公开的。为了让 Python 正常运行，你必须能够在线程之间共享数据。所以，是的，这是

cues.en: part of the package of the Golectomy. We don't have a problem here.
cues.zh: 无 GIL 改造配套的一部分。我们在这没有什么问题。

cues.en: C's extension parallelism and reentrancy, there's really no way around it. We're going to break code and it's kind of the point to change the interpreter and C extensions are going to break when they first try to run under the golectomy.
cues.zh: C 扩展的并行性和可重入性，这确实绕不过去。我们会破坏代码，而这正是改解释器的意义所在；C 扩展第一次在 GILectomy 下运行时就会坏掉。

cues.en: And as far as the atomicity of operations,
cues.zh: 至于操作的原子性，

cues.en: this is where we replace the one giant lock in Python with millions, and I literally mean millions of locks
cues.zh: 这就是我们把 Python 里那一把大锁换成数百万把锁的地方，我真的是说数百万把锁

cues.en: all over the place, little tiny locks.
cues.zh: 到处都是，一把把极小的锁。

cues.en: So there's going to be a new lock API, at least internally. That's what I've done in the Gillectomy.
cues.zh: 所以会有一个新的锁 API，至少内部会有。这就是我在 GILectomy 里做的事。

cues.en: I have macros called pylock and unlock that you use kind of like PyAnker and PyDecker.
cues.zh: 我有名为 pylock 和 unlock 的宏，用法有点像 Py_INCREF 和 Py_DECREF。

cues.en: Then the pytype object has sprouted an oblock method. I don't know if it's exposed yet. I expect it to someday be exposed to functions and probably called dunder lock and dunder unlock. Oh, sorry.
cues.zh: 然后 PyTypeObject 对象长出了一个 oblock 方法。我不知道它是否已经暴露。我预计有一天会暴露给函数，可能叫 __lock__ 和 __unlock__。哦，抱歉。

cues.en: So what objects need to be locked?
cues.zh: 那么哪些对象需要加锁？

cues.en: Any mutable object. And when I say mutable, I don't actually mean Python mutable, I mean C mutable. So consider, for instance, the str object. As Python programmers are like, Oh, strs are immutable. And of course they are. But internally inside of C Python, there are a bunch of lazily computed fields.
cues.zh: 任何可变对象。我说可变，其实不是指 Python 层面的可变，而是指 C 层面的可变。比如拿 str 对象来说。Python 程序员会说，哦，str 是不可变的。当然没错。但在 CPython 内部，有一堆惰性计算的字段。

cues.en: Like, for instance, the hash value. We don't know the hash when we start up.
cues.zh: 比如哈希值。启动时我们并不知道哈希值。

cues.en: It's actually we store a negative one as the hash value. That's why negative one is an illegal value for hash. So we store a negative one and we look and see, Oh, it's negative one right now. We need to compute the hash. If two threads came along and they both saw the negative one, they would both compute the hash and then both of them would override it. And in this case, it's not going to hurt anything, like two threads wasting a little time and overriding each other's values with the same computed value, that's fine. But there are two other fields, UTF-eight and Wstr, that are internal representations
cues.zh: 实际上我们会把 -1 存为哈希值。这就是为什么 -1 是哈希的非法值。所以我们存一个 -1，然后看一看，哦，现在它是 -1，我们需要计算哈希。如果两个线程过来，都看到 -1，它们都会计算哈希，然后都覆盖它。这种情况下不会造成伤害，比如两个线程浪费一点时间，用相同的计算结果互相覆盖，那没问题。但还有两个字段，UTF-8 和 wstr，它们是内部表示

cues.en: of the string. Those are computed lazily,
cues.zh: 字符串的。这些是惰性计算的，

cues.en: and those both allocate memory. And so if we had two threads that both computed those and overwrote,
cues.zh: 而且这两个都会分配内存。所以如果两个线程都计算了它们并覆盖，

cues.en: we're going to leak memory. That's bad. We would need some locking here. I don't know if we need a lock per string or some global locks or something,
cues.zh: 就会泄漏内存。那很糟。这里我们需要某种锁。我不知道是需要每个字符串一把锁，还是一些全局锁之类的，

cues.en: but eventually we're going need to lock str objects. I haven't done it right now, so you can't use strs very much inside of the Golectomy.
cues.zh: 但最终我们需要给 str 对象加锁。我现在还没做，所以在 GILectomy 里不能大量使用 str。

cues.en: Now, what kind of lock do you need? You need what I'm going to call a user space lock.
cues.zh: 那么，你需要什么样的锁呢？你需要我称之为用户态锁的东西。

cues.en: This is not technically... Like, people said, Oh, user space lock. That doesn't exist. What I mean here is this is a lock that only uses user space resources, like RAM,
cues.zh: 从技术上讲，这并不是……就像人们说的，哦，用户态锁，那根本不存在。我这里的意思是，这是一种只使用用户态资源（比如内存）的锁，

cues.en: until there is contention. At the point that you have contention, you're talking about threads and scheduling, you need to involve the kernel. And so you consume some kernel resources while there is contention. Once the contention is gone, those resources should go away and you're back to only consuming RAM.
cues.zh: 直到发生竞争。一旦出现竞争，就会涉及到线程和调度，你就需要内核介入。因此，在有竞争的时候会消耗一些内核资源。一旦竞争消失，这些资源就应该释放，然后你又回到了只消耗内存的状态。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: user space locks are pretty common, actually. Under Linux, have this wonderful thing called the Futex, which is a fast user space lock. It's not actually a lock, it's a lock primitive that you can use to make your own locking. And I'm doing all of my development under 64
cues.zh: 用户态锁其实非常普遍。在 Linux 下，有一个好东西叫 Futex，也就是快速用户态锁。它其实不是一个锁，而是一个用于构建你自己的锁的锁原语。我所有的开发都是在 64

cues.en: bit Linux, so this is what I've been using.
cues.zh: 位 Linux 下进行的，所以这就是我一直在使用的。

cues.en: Under Windows, there is a long standing thing called the critical section that I'm assured is user space only until there is contention,
cues.zh: 在 Windows 下，有一个历史悠久的东西叫临界区，据我所知它也是纯用户态的，直到发生竞争为止，

cues.en: and under
cues.zh: 而在

cues.en: OS X, I'm told that the standard
cues.zh: OS X 下，据说 POSIX 的标准

cues.en: PTHread library from POSIX, that PTHread mutex under OS X is a user space only lock until there's contention. So I think we're already good for a lot of the major platforms that we care about. And the other platforms, I don't know what the answers are. Again, it's very early days for the Golectomy.
cues.zh: pthread 库，即 OS X 下的 pthread 互斥锁，在发生竞争之前也是一个纯用户态锁。所以我想我们关心的许多主流平台基本上都已经支持了。至于其他平台，我不知道答案是什么。再说一次，Golectomy 现在还处于非常早期的阶段。

cues.en: I'm assuming that they have similar answers here as well.
cues.zh: 我假设他们这里也有类似的答案。

cues.en: Now, as far as these political constraints I talked about,
cues.zh: 现在，就我谈到的这些政治限制而言，

cues.en: I say that I can deliver a Golectomy branch that doesn't hurt single threaded performance and doesn't break C extensions. Now, may remember, mere slides ago, I said we made it 30% slower off the top and every c extension breaks. So how can I claim this?
cues.zh: 我说我可以提供一个 Golectomy 分支，它既不会损害单线程性能，也不会破坏 C 扩展。你们可能还记得，就在几页幻灯片之前，我说过我们一开始让它慢了 30%，而且每个 C 扩展都会出问题。那我怎么能这么说呢？

cues.en: The answer is we have two builds. You can build... If we ever merge this, and again, I don't know when it'll happen,
cues.zh: 答案是我们要有两种构建。你可以构建……如果我们最终合并这个，再说一次，我不知道什么时候会发生，

cues.en: we should be able to build Python both with the GIL and without the GIL, and the with GIL build would remain the default for probably a very long time.
cues.zh: 我们应该能够同时构建带 GIL 和不带 GIL 的 Python，而带 GIL 的构建可能在很长时间内仍是默认选项。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: with the GIL is what the Python we have today, and everything works exactly the same. Your c extensions still work, you still have the GIL, and your code doesn't break, which is great. And then for the crazy futurists,
cues.zh: 带 GIL 的就是我们今天用的 Python，一切运作完全相同。你的 C 扩展仍然能用，你仍然有 GIL，代码不会坏，这很好。然后对于疯狂的未来主义者，

cues.en: we can compile it without the GIL, and that's when things like locking start happening. So we would have these these are all macros in C, which means that we can compile them way into nothing. So pylock and pyunlock in the GIL build
cues.zh: 我们可以编译不带 GIL 的版本，那时候像加锁这样的事情就开始发生了。所以我们会有这些——这些在 C 里都是宏，意味着我们可以把它们编译成空。所以带 GIL 的构建里，pylock 和 pyunlock

cues.en: would do nothing. And without GIL build, they would now do something. So this means that we're complicating the CPython source code by having support for both with the GIL and without the GIL on different lines, and you're gonna have to read the code and understand in different contexts it means different things.
cues.zh: 什么也不做。而在不带 GIL 的构建里，它们就会起作用了。这意味着我们通过在不同行上同时支持带 GIL 和不带 GIL，把 CPython 的源代码复杂化了，你得读代码并理解在不同上下文中它意味着不同的东西。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: in order to keep some sanity in the world, I propose that we also have two entry points on shared libraries.
cues.zh: 为了让这个世界还能保持一点理智，我提议我们也给共享库提供两个入口点。

cues.en: So if you compile with the GIL, then you're gonna have the same entry point you have today for a shared library, for a C extension, and in the future you would have a different named entry point, which means that the without GIL build is strictly opt in.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你用 GIL 编译，那么共享库、C 扩展就还是今天这个入口点；而将来你会有一个不同名字的入口点，这意味着无 GIL 构建是严格选择启用的。

cues.en: This means that nobody's code breaks. You have to, as an extension author, you have to say, I'm ready for no GIL. Here's entry
cues.zh: 这意味着不会破坏任何人的代码。作为扩展作者，你必须明确表示：我已经准备好支持无 GIL 了。这里是入口

cues.en: point that you can call that means that you can load me in a no GIL build. This also has the nice feature of you can examine a shared library externally and determine whether or not it supports no GIL builds.
cues.zh: 点，你可以调用它，这意味着你可以在无 GIL 构建中加载我。这还有一个好处：你可以从外部检查一个共享库，判断它是否支持无 GIL 构建。

cues.en: It might be possible in the future. Again, I haven't explored this yet, but this is just sort of a note to myself.
cues.zh: 将来也许有可能。再说一次，我还没探索过这个，但这只是给自己记一笔。

cues.en: If we took those macros and turned them into C functions and allowed you to call into them, we might be able to make it so that you could write a single. So that supported both kinds of builds. And it would just be like, oh, you call this one when you're in noGil and you call that one when you're withGil,
cues.zh: 如果我们把这些宏变成 C 函数，并允许你调用它们，也许就能让你只写一个，同时支持两种构建。就像这样：你在 noGil 时调用这个，在 withGil 时调用那个，

cues.en: and you'd just have both of them in your code, kind of like we're going to have in C Python itself,
cues.zh: 然后你的代码里两个都有，差不多就像我们会在 CPython 本身里做的那样，

cues.en: and that would let the extension authors only compile once and not have to face as much complexity and just understand,
cues.zh: 这样扩展作者就只需要编译一次，不用面对那么多复杂度，只需要理解

cues.en: like, both. But they wouldn't have to compile it twice and ship two different binaries.
cues.zh: 两者，但他们不必编译两次并发布两个不同的二进制文件。

cues.en: Now, since effectively this is a new CAPI, it looks almost exactly like the existing CAPI,
cues.zh: 既然这实际上是一个新的 CAPI，它看起来几乎和现有的 CAPI 完全一样，

cues.en: but we have this new locking stuff and some of the semantics are different. Arguably, this is kind of a different CAPI, and so this might be a good opportunity to say, There are a bunch of things that are recommended practices in Python. These are best practices for C extension authors, but they're not required.
cues.zh: 但我们加入了这些新的加锁机制，而且部分语义也有所不同。可以说，这算是一个不太一样的 CAPI，因此这也可能是一个好机会，去表明：Python 中有很多推荐的做法。这些是针对 C 扩展开发者的最佳实践，但它们并不是强制的。

cues.en: And it hurts us because we have to support all this nasty old backwards compatibility behavior. This might be a good opportunity to shed that and say, You know what? Now, pytype ready, that's no longer optional. This is something it's possible to create a type in Python
cues.zh: 这让我们很头疼，因为我们必须支持所有这些讨厌的旧版向后兼容行为。这可能是一个甩掉它们的绝佳机会，心想：你知道吗？现在，pytype 就绪检查不再是可选的了。这就好比你可以在 Python 中创建一种类型，

cues.en: and introduce objects into the Python runtime without ever telling Python, Hey, I have a new type for you. This is what tells Python, I have a new type for you. We might say, Okay, it's required in no GIL builds.
cues.zh: 并把对象引入 Python 运行时，却完全不用告诉 Python：“嘿，我为你准备了一个新类型。” 这行代码就是用来告诉 Python：“我为你准备了一个新类型。” 我们也许会说：好吧，在无 GIL 构建中，这是必须的。

cues.en: PEP four eighty nine is this thing I don't quite understand, but it's multi phase C extension initialization.
cues.zh: PEP 489 这个东西我其实不是特别懂，但它指的是多阶段 C 扩展初始化。

cues.en: Again, it seems like it's a good idea. It might be a good time to say, That's not optional anymore either. Now remember when I said, Don't make it too complicated? This is kind of where the Gillectomy's falling down a little bit. Now we're going to have these two different builds. We're going to have code interleaved where this is with Gill and this is without Gill.
cues.zh: 同样，这听起来是个好主意。现在也许是个好时机宣布：这也再也不是可选的了。大家还记得我刚才说“别把它搞得太复杂”吗？这就是 Gillectomy（去GIL）稍微遇到点麻烦的地方。现在我们将拥有这两种不同的构建版本。我们的代码将交织在一起，一部分有 GIL，一部分没有 GIL。

cues.en: People have said, We can live with this, Larry, if you can make it fast enough.
cues.zh: 大家曾对我说：“Larry，只要你能让它足够快，我们就能接受。”

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: I have been working on this for a couple of months. My original code name was Confuse a Cat, then I thought of Gallectomy, and I was like, Oh, no, that's the name. We're done.
cues.zh: 我为此已经研究了好几个月。我最初的代码名叫“迷惑猫咪”，后来想到了“Gallectomy”，当时我就觉得，哦，不，这就是那个名字。搞定收工。

cues.en: So I've gone back a lot of times to this essay that Guido wrote in 2007 titled It Isn't Easy to Remove the Gil on his Old Arma Block, and I've reread it and reread it, and I keep finding new things that he said.
cues.zh: 所以我经常回看Guido在2007年写的那篇题为《在他旧的Arma Block上移除GIL并不容易》的文章，我读了一遍又一遍，不断发现他当时说过的新内容。

cues.en: It's really worth reading, and I agree with everything that he says except the title.
cues.zh: 这真的非常值得一读，除了标题之外，我赞同他说的每一句话。

cues.en: Because it turns out, if you know where to start, you can actually remove the GIL in about a week.
cues.zh: 因为事实证明，如果你知道从哪里入手，大约一周就能把GIL移除掉。

cues.en: So here is the list of all the things you need to do in order to remove the GIL. Step zero, switch a PI Anchor and PI Decker to atomic Anchor and Decker. That's real easy. Step two, step one, I should say,
cues.zh: 那么，这就是移除GIL所需完成的所有事情列表。第零步，将PI Anchor和PI Decker切换为原子的Anchor和Decker。这非常简单。第二步，或者我应该说第一步，

cues.en: decide on what locking mechanism you're gonna use.
cues.zh: 决定你要使用什么锁机制。

cues.en: It has to be recursive.
cues.zh: 它必须是可重入的（recursive）。

cues.en: It has to be user space only because you're going to have a lot of them.
cues.zh: 它必须仅限用户空间，因为你会用到很多这样的锁。
